sentences: `M = op(M, DATA)` on the 64-bit element at the MUBUF address (two dwords, low first); with `glc` the old 64 bits are returned in `vdata[0:1]`.
Each dword is its own 32-bit `OpAtomic*`, so no Int64 atomics are needed; a bitwise op leaves the same memory that way, since its bits are independent.

**Approximation:** an exchange can tear, since two lanes swapping into one element at once can leave one's low dword with the other's high dword (A.lo, B.lo, B.hi, A.hi), and the returned pair comes from two reads, so another lane's 64-bit op on the same element between them can show up half done.
**Bounds:** the check covers the whole 8-byte element, all or nothing, as for a typed 32_32 element (`buffer_address(elem="fmt")`).
An out-of-range or inactive lane leaves memory alone and returns 0, as `buffer_atomic` does.
How hardware treats a 64-bit atomic that is only partly in range is **not measured**.
Until 2026-11-22 every `_x2` buffer atomic was rejected.

CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_buffer_atomics_x2.py` (the four ops with and without `glc`, an element ending exactly at `num_records`, half and fully out of range, seeded values, rejected forms).
